newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore regional investments up sharply in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Singapore regional investments up sharply in 1996.

text.p: Singapore's investments in eight Asian countries in 1996 ran sharply ahead of 1995, the Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Tuesday.
Although full-year figures were available for just two of the countries, the data already showed the city-state's 1996 investments up 22 percent or U.S.$1.77 billion from 1995 to $8.06 billion.
For 1995 as a whole, investments in the eight countries -- Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, the Philippines, China, Vietnam, Burma and India -- were $6.29 billion.
Indonesia, with figures for all of 1996 available, topped the list with investments of $3.1 billion.
China had $987 million registered during the first half of the year compared with $1.86 billion for all of 1995. Singapore remained the fifth largest investor in China, the EDB said.

Thailand showed $1.06 billion in investments over the first nine months and Malaysia $1.32 billion over the first eight. The Malaysian figure was up from $403.5 million for all of 1995. Singapore was Malaysia's top foreign investor, the EDB said.
Singapore investments into ASEAN countries totalled $7.01 billion in 1996 according to data thus far available.
"ASEAN countries absorbed the bulk of Singapore's foreign direct investments," EDB director for international business development Chua Taik Him said at a news briefing.
"With the healthy and rapid growth of the ASEAN economies and the ASEAN Free Trade Area approaching, the confidence of Singapore-based investors in the region was boosted."
ASEAN -- Association of South East Asian Nations -- comprises Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei, the Philippines, Thailand and Singapore.
EDB said the number of regional investment projects, mostly by Singapore companies, increased by 16.3 percent for all of 1996, with 443 projects compared with 381 in 1995.
China has the lion's share with 166, followed by South Asia (94), Indochina (93), ASEAN (89) and others (1).

Manufacturing and services remained the most important sectors, with 318 projects in manufacturing in 1996 compared with 250 in 1995, and 71 projects in services, up from 53. Infrastructural projects saw a decline to 41 from 58 in 1995.

Chua said in the next regionalisation stage, EDB would stress developing resources and enterprises by enhancing regional linkages, providing comprehensive support for local companies, developing competent manpower and improving Singapore's relevance to regional strategies of multinational companies.
